_comment: klt erc supply spec for the digital UTMI PHY's routed GDS -- the T1
item 11 (power delivery, structural) artifact for this repo (issue
#77). Follows gf180-drone-fc's layout/digital/erc-supply-spec.json
worked example, re-derived from this block's own GDS rather than
copied from another PDK's spec.
Run it against the committed routed GDS:
klt erc layout/digital/usb_utmi_phy.gds \
layout/digital/erc-supply-spec.json --top usb_utmi_phy \
--format json
What this spec asserts, and why each piece is shaped this way:
- `stackup[0]` MUST carry `"role": "gate"` (klt erc's own
contract), so the stack starts at Poly2 rather than at a metal.
`active_layer` (Comp 22/0) makes the gate denominator `poly n diff`
instead of raw poly area, which is what keeps the filltie/endcap/
filler-cell poly bars -- real poly with no gate oxide -- out of
`gates[]` entirely instead of reporting non-physical antenna
ratios for them (klayout-tools docs/cli/erc.md, 'Gate area').
This routed GDS contains 854 such physical-only instances per the
digital-lvs record, so the exclusion is load-bearing here.
- Metal1-Metal5 are the full gf180mcu 5-metal stack (34/0, 36/0,
42/0, 46/0, 81/0). The P&R power grid's straps run on Metal1
(followpins), Metal4 and Metal5
(flow/request-usb-utmi-phy-par.json -> power.straps), and item
11's Digital column requires every `power.straps[].layer` to be
covered by this spec's own stackup -- Metal1, Metal4, Metal5 all
are.
- `label_layer` is declared ONLY on the two layers this block's
merged GDS actually puts supply text on, verified by reading the
GDS's own text inventory rather than assuming:
- Metal1 `34/10`: 330 texts, of which 64 `VDD` + 64 `VSS` are the
standard cells' own PG pin labels across the cell rows.
- Metal5 `81/10`: exactly 2 texts -- one `VDD`, one `VSS` -- the
PDN's top-level supply pin text.
Metal2 text `36/10` carries 35 signal-pin-only texts (`DataIn[0]`
..., zero supply text), so declaring it there would add nothing;
Metal3/Metal4 carry no text layer entries in this GDS at all.
(The remaining 10-datatype texts are unrelated to supply nets:
21/10 carries 62 `VNW` and 204/10 carries 62 `VPW` well-tap
labels -- well/substrate ties, not the routed VDD/VSS rails, and
`klt erc` has no stackup role for a well.)
- GDS layer numbers are gf180mcu's own drawn layers, derived from
the PDK's own libs.tech/klayout/tech/gf180mcu.lyp (COMP 22/0,
Poly2 30/0, Contact 33/0, Metal1 34/0, Via1 35/0, Metal2 36/0,
Metal5 81/0; label datatypes Metal1_Label 34/10, Metal2_Label
36/10, Metal5_Label 81/10) and cross-checked against
klayout-tools' curated gf180mcu deck layer table
(src/klayout_tools/decks/gf180mcu.py) -- identical.
- `nets[]`: VDD and VSS both `kind: "supply"`, which is what makes
a short between them report as the severe `erc.supply_short`
rather than the general `erc.multiply_driven_net`. Each must
resolve to exactly ONE electrical island: `erc.unconnected_net`
fires on zero matches (nothing in the layout carries that label
at all) AND on more than one (the rail is split into pieces that
never touch) -- so ZERO findings of that rule naming a declared
supply is exactly the 'one island per supply' verdict, not merely
an absence. The split-rail case is precisely the no-PDN failure
mode this spec exists to detect.
- There is deliberately NO `ties[]` section here, and that is a
recorded gap rather than an oversight: declaring one on a real
routed standard-cell layout collapses the design into one
electrical island and reports a FALSE `erc.supply_short` --
filed upstream as klayout-tools#2169, reproduced four ways in
gf180-drone-fc's FRICTION F-034. Because `ties[]` is omitted,
`erc.missing_tie` is NOT COMPUTED by this run (klayout-tools
docs/cli/erc.md: 'Omitted entirely -> erc.missing_tie is never
computed') -- its absence from the committed report is an absence
of evidence, not evidence of absence. The well-tie evidence that
does stand in for it, named per issue #77:
`power.tapcell_master: gf180mcu_fd_sc_mcu9t5v0__filltie` in the
committed place-and-route output (the routed DEF carries a real
SPECIALNETS VDD/VSS grid), the 62 `VNW` + 62 `VPW` well-tap
labels drawn in this GDS (21/10, 204/10 -- the standard-cell
rows' tap stacks), and the 64+64 VDD/VSS PG pin labels on
34/10. Still missing, tracked as its own gap: an LVS report
whose `power_connectivity.status` reads `"match"` -- the
committed digital-lvs record predates that field.
